draft.title: Operant conditioning
card: Operant conditioning is learning by the consequences of a behaviour. A person or animal links what they do with what happens next.
It is described in three phases: antecedent, behaviour, consequence. The antecedent is what comes before the behaviour. The consequence is what follows it.
a consequence that makes the behaviour more likely to happen again.
a consequence that makes the behaviour less likely to happen again.
draft.remember: The consequence shapes what happens next time: reinforcement makes a behaviour more likely, punishment less likely.

a.q: Jai's teacher says 'Begin your task'. Jai starts work and is praised, and he then starts work faster in later lessons. What is the praise?
opts: A consequence that is a reinforcement
An antecedent that is a reinforcement
A consequence that is a punishment
An antecedent that is a punishment
a.why: The praise comes after the behaviour, so it is the consequence. It made the behaviour more likely, so it is reinforcement. The teacher's instruction came before the behaviour, so it is the antecedent.
a.clue: Did the praise come before or after Jai started work, and did the behaviour increase?

b.q: Priya's dog jumps up at visitors when the doorbell rings. When visitors turn away and ignore the dog, it jumps up less often. Which statement is correct?
opts: The reaction is a punishment, as jumping became less likely
The doorbell is the antecedent, as it comes before jumping
The reaction is a reinforcement, as jumping became less likely
The jumping is the antecedent, as it leads to the reaction
b.why: The visitors' reaction follows the jumping and makes it less likely, so it is a punishment. The doorbell is the antecedent because it comes before the behaviour. The jumping is the behaviour, not the antecedent.
b.clue: Decide which phase each event is in, then check whether the behaviour became more or less likely.
